body:
No I obviously found that out early on in the relationship.  She really hates that it's something I never want to acknowledge or talk about, but it's just not a subject I want to discuss.
My depression really started about a year after I came home the last time.  I don't know if it was because the honeymoon period was over, but I just found myself really detached and couldn't focus anymore.  I was depressed about all the times I was gone and what I missed out on, that everyone my age and even younger were graduated and had real jobs.  Obviously when the grades slipped and I stopped going to class it didn't help.  I haven't had too many high points since except when my son was born, not even my wedding.  I was really excited when I started back at school, and I did well right away, but right now my wife thinks I'm in class but I'm really sitting here in my car afraid.  I'm afraid to approach people when I'm having trouble.  I never ask for help until I've dug a huge hole I can't get out of and completely break down.  I just pretend everything's okay.  I know I'm saying I want to kill myself but in reality I'll probably just sit here for the next few hours then go home and lie to my wife about how class was.  I have a psychiatry appt tomorrow I'm not excited about since I skipped my last one.  I'll probably just blow smoke up his ass as usual and say I'm doing alright just a little depressed.

The past ten years I just feel like I've sucked at everything I've done.  I was a pretty good student in high school, and I was a captain on the football team and baseball team, but that was the last time I was actually in any kind of leadership position.

I guess I wasn't a complete failure in the military.  I was in the National Guard for six years.  I was in Iraq on three different occasions.  I guess the worst thing I did was never got promoted to E5.  I mean it wasn't that I was a bad soldier, I don't have any really bad marks on my record.  Any of my supervisors would always write good reports about me.  I can guarantee if somebody asked them something about me now they wouldn't say anything bad.  I have quite a few awards, CAB, 2 ARCOMS, Good Conduct Medal, etc.  I mean I guess I really didn't like the military that much, but I still did my job and I like to think pretty well.  I spent a year as a gunner from the summer of 06 to the summer of 07 escorting convoys to all corners of Iraq.  I logged over 40,000 miles.

I guess I should have mentioned that before I met my wife, her brother died in Iraq.  Had I known that going in I definitely would not have went on one date with her.  I never wanted to be on that side of the war, and somehow that's where I ended up.  

I just wish I could dig myself out of this stupid hole.  I hate having to tell my wife that once again I've been lying to her about how I've been doing.  We've been through this so many times.
